item.title: Optical signatures of Rashba--Dresselhaus coupling across Franz--Keldysh and Landau regimes in two-dimensional semiconductors
item.description: arXiv:2610.31843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified theory of the interband optical response of a two-dimensional semiconductor with simultaneous Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings in electric and magnetic fields. In crossed fields, the in-plane electric field generates an effective spin-orbit drift field that modifies the Landau spectrum and spinor states, while at zero magnetic field the problem maps onto Landau--Zener spin dynamics.At zero external fields, the total joint density of states above the band gap remains unchanged, while characteristic subgap structures appear. Pure Rashba coupling produces an inverse square root singularity, whereas a finite Dresselhaus term gives a step and a logarithmic peak, allowing the two couplings to be distinguished optically. At zero magnetic field, the Franz--Keldysh response shows a crossover from diabatic to adiabatic spin dynamics as the electric field is reduced. In the weak-field Rashba regime, the field-free singularity becomes a finite peak whose height scales as $\mathcal E^{-1/3}$ and whose position approaches $E_g-E_{\rm SO}$, providing a direct measure of the Rashba energy. In a perpendicular magnetic field, spin-orbit coupling shifts and splits the Landau absorption lines and produces anticrossings without changing their total weights. The Rashba splitting changes from a $\sqrt{B}$ dependence at weak fields to a linear dependence at strong fields. Finally, in crossed electric and magnetic fields, the electric field broadens the Landau lines and drives a continuous crossover toward the Franz--Keldysh regime, while spin-orbit coupling produces opposite shifts and different widths for the two members of each doublet.
item.dc:creator: Bahruz Suleymanli, Samir Tariverdiev, B. Tanatar

item.title: Heat current and noise in a point-like junction between normal metal and fractional quantum hall edge state with $\nu = 1/3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we investigate heat current correlations between two edge states coupled through a constriction in the fractional quantum Hall regime at filling factor $\nu = 1/3$. This configuration allows us to map the system onto an interacting Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid with a local impurity, where the interaction parameter takes the value $\kappa = 1/2$. This specific parameter value enables the application of the refermionization method. By solving the refermionized Hamiltonian, we compute the heat current and evaluate the finite-frequency heat auto- and cross-correlation functions. Our results reveal asymmetric behavior with frequency, corresponding to absorption and emission noise, respectively. Furthermore, we examine several limiting cases, including low- and high-temperature limits as well as strong- and weak-backscattering regimes. In the weak backscattering regime, the Lorenz number approaches $4L_0$ at high voltage, suggesting a rescaling of the Wiedemann-Franz law due to interactions. A detailed study of the heat current fluctuations has made it possible to identify and derive expressions for the dominant contribution in the various regimes of interest, and to reveal the predominance of partition noise.
item.dc:creator: Redouane Zamoum, Houssam Eddine Farhi, Abdellah Touati, Adeline Cr\'epieux

item.title: Visualization of Single Spin-chain Propagation using Bragg Coherent Diffraction Imaging
item.description: arXiv:2610.31919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Domain wall dynamics and their manipulation in finite-size systems serve as a promising platform for beyond Moore's law applications. Yet, the imaging techniques to track their motion in real-space and time are limited. Here, we use magnetic domain walls formed in permalloy artificial square lattice to demonstrate that single-shot Bragg coherent diffraction imaging (BCDI) is a powerful approach for this purpose. Our BCDI reconstructed images revealed milliseconds time-scale dynamics of the antiphase magnetic domain walls traveling through an antiferromagnetically ordered sample.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoqian M. Chen, Justin S. Woods, Ulrich Welp, Wai-kwong Kwok, Ralu Divan, David A. Czaplewski, Scott Dhuey, Sujoy Roy, Rajesh V. Chopdekar, Lance E. De Long, Andi Barbour, Claudio Mazzoli, Ian Robinson, J. Todd Hastings

item.title: Dipole chains of Bloch point singularities revealed by X-ray magnetic tomography
item.description: arXiv:2610.31952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bloch point singularities play an important role in magnetic systems, mediating changes in topology in three dimensional configurations. However, until now they have only been observed as isolated objects or as part of individual topological textures. Here we present the experimental observation of a 1D dipole chain of Bloch points in an anisotropic chiral magnet using soft X-ray magnetic vector tomography. We identify that the chain of Bloch point singularities lies along a boundary between regions of opposite chirality and that neighbouring Bloch and anti-Bloch points are stable at separations down to 60 nm. The stability of the Bloch points is determined to be closely related to the surrounding topology of the magnetisation configuration and a threshold separation for the spontaneous annihilation of Bloch point-anti-Bloch point pairs within chiral domain walls is identified to be approximately 90 nm in distance. This observation of a chain of Bloch points and the insight into their stability, offers a route to explore the correlative behaviour of such topological point defects. The behaviour and control of such point defects is of relevance for the control of 3D magnetisation configurations, and provides a new route towards the creation of correlated configurations of singularities in a magnetic system.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Neethirajan, Rikako Yamamoto, Marisel Di Pietro Mart\'inez, Luke A. Turnbull, Praveen Vir, Chandra Shekar, Claudia Felser, Luis Carlos Colocho Hurtarte, Benedikt J. Daurer, Majid Kazemian, Burkhard Kaulich, Claire Donnelly

item.title: The Extended Diode Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.32090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For more than 75 years, the p-n junction current-voltage characteristic has been derived by treating majority carriers as an inert background and conflating the junction voltage with the applied bias. Here we show that the base electric field, generated by the coupling of excess majority and minority carriers, fundamentally alters the internal potential distribution. This self-consistent framework yields a closed-form extended diode equation that reproduces the high-injection roll-off without invoking an external series resistance, thereby eliminating an empirical patch that has persisted in the classical theory.
item.dc:creator: Jianhong Yang, Gonghao Sun, Tinglan Li

item.title: A Self-Consistent Two-Carrier Drift-Diffusion Framework for p-n Junctions: Extended Diode Equation, Power Dissipation, and Base Transit Time
item.description: arXiv:2610.32112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical theory of p-n junctions derives the current-voltage characteristic from minority-carrier diffusion alone: majority carriers are treated as an inert background, the quasi-neutral base as field-free, and the junction voltage as equal to the applied bias. These premises fail together under high bias and high-level injection, where the observed current roll-off is reproduced only by appending an empirical series resistance outside the junction physics. Here we develop a self-consistent two-carrier drift-diffusion framework that introduces no assumption beyond the classical ones. Excess majority carriers are shown to be electrostatically forced transport participants: the ambipolar diffusion equation, closed by exact two-sided boundary conditions, yields a unified excess-carrier profile. The resulting base field separates into an ohmic and a Dember component, and all four current components follow in closed form, their sum being position independent. At device level the framework closes into an extended diode equation that contains the Shockley equation as its low-injection, long-base limit and reproduces the n=2 roll-off intrinsically. The junction voltage emerges as a self-limiting drop confined to the space-charge region and separated from the applied bias by exact base drops. Two device-level corrections are quantified: at high current, 75-90% of the dissipation migrates from the junction into the quasi-neutral base, and field-assisted acceleration shortens the base transit time by up to a factor of six. Three parameter-free predictions follow: a universal ideality-factor crossover that passes through 3/2 when the boundary excess equals the doping, a high-injection onset voltage that scales as 119 mV per decade of doping, and a geometry factor that survives into high injection.
item.dc:creator: Jianhong Yang, Tinglan Li, Gonghao Sun

item.title: Material criteria for angular-momentum transfer from twisted photons to photoelectrons
item.description: arXiv:2610.32121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an $n$-type semiconductor surface. Within a single-valley effective-mass model of surface photoemission, we calculate OAM-resolved spectra for GaAs, InSb, $\mathrm{InAs}_{0.34}\mathrm{Sb}_{0.66}$, and $\mathrm{Hg}_{0.76}\mathrm{Cd}_{0.24}\mathrm{Te}$ irradiated by twisted photons with Laguerre--Gaussian--like momentum profile. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. Efficient transfer requires the transverse momentum of the conduction electron to be much smaller than the transverse momentum width of the photon, which favors low temperatures, small conduction-band effective masses, and shallow donor levels. GaAs is less favorable within the present model because of its larger effective mass and deeper donor levels. We also discuss the demanding photon-wave packet parameters, possible extensions to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and post-emission OAM selection. Although the generation of vortex electrons with a vanishing OAM uncertainty via photoemission seems challenging, we argue that it is still possible to generate single-electron vortex states with a finite OAM dispersion.
item.dc:creator: A. A. Shchepkin, D. V. Karlovets

item.title: Magnonic time crystal with lasing coherence
item.description: arXiv:2610.32199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete time crystals (DTC) can respond at an integer multiple of the drive period. Internal order-parameter measurements have advanced studies of this novel non-equilibrium phase of matter; however, turning this order into highly coherent, externally accessible radiation remains challenging: pump-driven nonlinear processes must supply sufficient gain to compensate dissipation while preserving subharmonic stability. Here we realize a room-temperature magnonic time crystal (MTC) with radiation of lasing coherence using a pump-induced magnon mode in yttrium iron garnet. A microwave beat drive produces robust period doubling over a finite parameter range, with spectral signatures of higher-order MTC at stronger driving. The emitted field exhibits linewidth narrowing to 260.0 Hz and a first-order correlation decay time of $995 \mu s$. Our model links this response to three-magnon confluence, yields a stability region consistent with experiment and predicts a possible transition to chaos. We further map the complex temporal dynamics into frequency-resolved nonlinear features for reservoir computing. These results bridge time-crystalline order and nonlinear information processing through intrinsic magnon-magnon interactions and lasing coherence.
item.dc:creator: Jiantao Song, C. K. Wei, Shuhuan Ma, Yiming Pan, Zhijian Chen, Li Yu, Wei Lu, Bimu Yao

item.title: Nonlocal Thermoelectric Transport in Degenerate Electron Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When the characteristic length scales of transport become comparable to the carrier mean free path, the local constitutive description breaks down. We develop the Flux Derivative Formalism (FDF), a kinetic framework that provides a systematic route from the Boltzmann equation to nonlocal constitutive equations. We use it to derive coupled equations for charge and heat transport in isotropic electronic systems, together with boundary conditions derived consistently within this approach, yielding a closed macroscopic description that can be applied to complex geometries without solving the full Boltzmann problem. The explicit transport coefficients are derived for degenerate electronic systems within the Callaway model. A central result is that varying the relative strength of resistive and momentum-conserving collisions changes the transport coefficients but not the non-local constitutive structure, providing a continuous description from resistive-dominated transport to the collective hydrodynamic limit. The electronic heat equation takes a Guyer-Krumhansl form, whose predictions are validated against size-dependent thermal-transport measurements in Cu and Ni. For coupled thermoelectric transport, the resulting boundary-value problem determines the complete geometry-dependent transport matrix. Comparison with spatially resolved Boltzmann solutions confirms quantitative accuracy down to transverse dimensions comparable to the carrier mean free path. The theory predicts geometry-dependent Seebeck and Peltier coefficients while preserving Onsager reciprocity and the Kelvin relation.
item.dc:creator: Albert Beardo, Adri\'an Ramos-Mart\'in, Jordi Tur-Prats, F. Xavier Alvarez, Juan Camacho

item.title: Quantum Landau Lifshitz Gilbert equation in ferromagnetic conductors and magnetic insulators
item.description: arXiv:2610.32405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the microscopic origin of magnetic damping is essential for describing magnetization dynamics in nanoscale magnetic systems. In this work, we develop a microscopic framework to derive Gilbert damping terms from specific interactions in ferromagnetic conductors and magnetic insulators. In ferromagnetic conductors, magnetic damping is dominated by the s d exchange interaction between the localized magnetic moments and the itinerant electrons, which is effectively equivalent to an electronmagnon interaction. From the spin diffusion equation and the spin transfer torque therein, we obtain the corresponding quantum LLG equation. In magnetic insulators, where free electrons are absent, spin phonon interactions become the primary source of the damping.Starting from an effective spin phonon interaction and using linear response theory, we derive a quantum LLG equation with a Gilbert damping tensor analytically. Our results demonstrate that different microscopic interactions lead to qualitatively different structures of magnetic damping. Instead of being described by a universal scalar parameter, Gilbert damping can exhibit spatial dependence and tensorial characteristics determined by the underlying microscopic interactions.
item.dc:creator: Ji Yang Zhu, Zheng Chuan Wang

item.title: Multifractal Magnons Around Localized Defects
item.description: arXiv:2610.32457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multifractal wavefunctions fluctuate over a hierarchy of spatial scales, remaining spatially extended while exhibiting strongly nonuniform structure. We show that magnons in otherwise crystalline two-dimensional magnets can exhibit such behavior on mesoscopic scales, without disorder or quasiperiodicity. A localized defect can mix discrete groups of nearly degenerate magnon states in a finite sample, generating multiscale interference patterns and multifractal wavefunctions. We demonstrate this mechanism for both a simple spin defect and topological magnetic skyrmions. Large-scale spin-wave calculations for skyrmions in chiral and frustrated magnets reveal clear multifractal diagnostics over the full accessible range of system sizes of above-gap modes. Crucially, skyrmions make these states experimentally observable by hybridizing them with magnetically active internal deformation modes, which gives a subset of the multifractal states a nonzero magnetic dipole moment. These states can therefore be excited by uniform ac fields and remain distinguishable at realistic frequency resolution, providing a direct route to observing mesoscopic magnon multifractality.
item.dc:creator: Adarsh Hullahalli, Yusuf Khand, Christos Panagopoulos, Christina Psaroudaki

item.title: Excitonic Stark Response Induced by Quantum Capacitance in van der Waals Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2610.32532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precise electrostatic control in van der Waals heterostructures is commonly described by a geometric capacitor model, which assumes that the internal electric field is fully determined by external gate voltages. Here, we show that this description breaks down in the presence of interfacial charge transfer, where quantum capacitance modifies the internal electrostatics. Using interlayer excitons as local probes, we observe a dipole-dependent energy splitting that persists even when the gate-induced geometric field is nominally canceled. This splitting reflects incomplete cancellation between gate- and carrier-induced fields set by quantum capacitance, while many-body renormalization is largely symmetric with respect to the two opposite dipole orientations, allowing the splitting to provide a direct optical measure of the local chemical potential. Our results reveal the central role of quantum capacitance in interface electrostatics and provide a route to probe it in operando.
item.dc:creator: Xiangzhi Hong, Yongkang Jian, Yang Chen, Rukai Cang, Yuanlong Guo, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Baigeng Wang, Erfu Liu

item.title: Magnetic Anisotropy and Magnetization Dynamics in Si/Ni Multilayers Probed by FMR and VSM Magnetometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.32565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The magnetic anisotropy and magnetization dynamics of sputtered [Si(40~\AA)/Ni($t_{\mathrm{Ni}}$~\AA)]$_{20}$ multilayers were systematically investigated at room temperature using SQUID--VSM magnetometry and angle-dependent ferromagnetic resonance (FMR). Static measurements reveal soft ferromagnetic behaviour in thicker Ni layers and mixed ferromagnetic and superparamagnetic contributions at reduced thicknesses. The saturation magnetization increases toward the bulk Ni value with increasing thickness, consistent with Ni nanocrystallite growth. Magnetic dead-layer analysis yields an interfacial dead-layer thickness of approximately $9$~\AA\ per interface, accounting for the suppressed magnetization in thinner Ni layers. Angle-dependent FMR measurements reveal effective easy-plane magnetic anisotropy, while out-of-plane spectra exhibit additional non-uniform spin-wave modes. The effective magnetization remains lower than the static saturation magnetization, indicating a perpendicular anisotropy contribution that partially compensates the demagnetizing field. Quantitative anisotropy analysis yields an interfacial anisotropy constant of $K_S = +0.17~\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-2}}$, favouring perpendicular magnetization, and a volume anisotropy constant of $K_V = -1.23 \times 10^6~\mathrm{erg\,cm^{-3}}$, favouring in-plane alignment, with an extrapolated anisotropy crossover thickness of $t_c \approx 27$~\AA. Increasing FMR line-shape asymmetry with decreasing Ni thickness is consistent with enhanced interfacial roughness. These findings highlight the competing interfacial and volume anisotropies and the importance of Ni thickness and interface quality in tailoring Si/Ni multilayers for silicon-compatible spintronic applications.
item.dc:creator: Dushyant Singh, Subha Maity, Tharundev V V, Subhavenkadesh SS, Vigneshwari SR, Krista R. Khiangte

item.title: Nano-ARPES observation of a flat band at the \bar{M} point in 2.4{\deg} twisted bilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2610.32714v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at the so-called magic angle reveals a range of intriguing phases, such as superconductivity and Mott insulating states, resulting from electrons entering a correlated state. This establishes twisted bilayer graphene as an excellent platform for exploring correlation effects in many-body phases and across various twist angles. However, in most cases, the twist angle is not an easy parameter to control because it exhibits structural instabilities such as relaxation and reconstruction that reduce the correlation effects. Here, we report the unexpected appearance of a flat band at the \bar{M} point far from the Fermi level in a 2.4{\deg} twisted bilayer graphene, directly visualized by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. Our work is the first observation of flat bands away from the \bar{K} point in twisted bilayer graphene and highlights the need to probe the entire Brillouin zone to fully capture electronic states in twisted structures.
item.dc:creator: Giovanna Feraco, Przemys{\l}aw Przybysz, Oreste De Luca, Ying Wang, Pavel Dudin, Jos\'e Avila, Jianting Ye, Pawe{\l} D\k{a}browski, Pawe{\l} J. Kowalczyk, Jagoda S{\l}awi\'nska, Petra Rudolf, Antonija Grubi\v{s}i\'c-\v{C}abo

item.title: First- and Second-Order Electron Position Correlators Reveal Topological Phase Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The theory of conventional critical phenomena is built around the concepts of fluctuations and correlators of local observables. Here, we show that topological phase transitions can also be characterized through spatial and temporal two-point correlation functions associated with fluctuations of the electronic position operator. The key object is the antisymmetric part of the position-position correlation function, which yields the Chern number in the equal-time and equal-space limit. When the system is translationally invariant in space or time (the latter case corresponding to an equilibrium condition), these two-point correlators reduce to one-variable functions of the remaining variable. Remarkably, these functions are both reminiscent of critical behaviour, including divergent correlation times and lengths signalling the phase transitions. Away from these conditions, namely in non-periodic systems or genuinely dynamical processes, criticality is instead better captured by higher-order Chern-Chern correlators constructed from local or dynamical markers obtained as coincident-point limits of the position correlators. These higher-order Chern-Chern correlators can be seen as double Levi-Civita contractions of second-order position correlators, selecting the antisymmetric sector in each index pair. We substantiate this framework through numerical simulations and analytic calculations. Our results establish a general correlator-based description of topological phase transitions, applicable to crystalline, noncrystalline, equilibrium, and dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Antimo Marrazzo, Christian Loer Llemit, Massimo Capone

item.title: Spontaneous Decay of High Energy Composite Fermions
item.description: arXiv:2610.32763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An electron, when added to a fractional quantum Hall fluid, famously splits into fractionally charged composite-fermion quasiparticles. We show here that a high energy composite fermion carrying a fractional charge decays into a collection of particles, including quasiparticles, quasiholes, and even whole electrons.
item.dc:creator: Mytraya Gattu, J. K. Jain

item.title: Floquet Engineering of Momentum Gaps in Magnonic Time Crystals: Slow-Drive Amplification and In-Gap Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2610.32766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic time crystals host momentum gaps in which waves grow exponentially but cannot propagate. We establish their magnonic counterpart in a thin film with periodically switched anisotropy, deriving its Floquet band structure and confirming it micromagnetically. Gaps require a precession-ellipticity contrast. The waveform controls high-order gaps: a single 1~GHz switching drive amplifies a comb of spin-wave bands, from 2.5 to 4.5~GHz, above Gilbert losses even with smoothed edges, unlike sinusoidal modulation. With the Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction, amplified packets propagate inside the gap while growing.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Gruszecki, Victor Pacheco-Pe\~na

item.title: Magnons and excitons from Bethe-Salpeter equation and its application to graphene-based magnets
item.description: arXiv:2610.32847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the recent isolation of two-dimensional semiconducting magnetic materials, the theoretical study of spin-flip collective excitations (magnons) along with spin-conserving electron-hole bound pairs (excitons) has become particularly relevant. Describing both types of quasiparticles within the same theoretical framework is possible, in principle, but the well-established many-body formalism for the calculation of excitons, based on the intertwined Bethe-Salpeter and Hedin's equations, is not satisfactory for magnons, since the usual approximations produce a spurious gapped Goldstone mode. Here, we show that excitons and magnons can be computed on the same footing under the same Bethe-Salpeter formalism, while respecting the gapless Goldstone mode for magnons. We demonstrate how this can be achieved through the evaluation of the full Bethe-Salpeter equation, beyond the Tamm-Dancoff approximation in model Hamiltonians. As an example, we apply it to ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic graphene, faithfully represented by the extended Hubbard model. Our results clarify the roles of on-site and non-local interactions in exciton and magnon appearance and identify consistency requirements relevant to extending the approach to first-principles calculations.
item.dc:creator: Simran Chourasia, Maur\'icio F. C. Martins Quintela, J. J. Palacios

item.title: Configuration-Independent Low-Energy Gaps in Graphene Nanoribbons: A $\delta$-Scatterer Transfer-Matrix Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.32901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transport measurements on lithographically patterned graphene nanoribbons suggest that the gap depends primarily on ribbon width rather than on crystallographic edge orientation, in contrast to predictions of ideal tight-binding models. To address this, we develop a transfer-matrix approach, based on the theory of finite periodic systems, in which each carbon atom of the honeycomb lattice is represented by an individual $\delta$-scatterer with interaction strength $\gamma^{}_{\delta}$ and the nanoribbon is treated as a confined multichannel finite periodic system. We derive the unit-cell transfer matrix for both arm-chair and zig-zag edge configurations and obtain the transmission and channel-coupling coefficients in closed form. The transmission spectra display the resonant band structure characteristic of finite periodic systems, with the number of resonances per allowed band increasing with the number of unit cells. For $\gamma_{\delta}=0$ the ribbons are fully transparent; for $\gamma_{\delta}>0$ a low-energy transport gap opens and grows linearly with the scatterer strength, $\Delta=0.364265\,\gamma_{\delta}$, identically for arm-chair and zig-zag edges. These results are consistent with the reported absence of a systematic dependence on orientation, while the analytical results show that interchannel coupling vanishes exactly for arm-chair ribbons and decreases with increasing width for zig-zag ribbons, revealing the role of edge geometry. Together, these findings indicate that atomic-scale scattering, represented by the $\delta$-potential formalism, provides a common orientation-independent contribution to the low-energy transport gap in the pristine ribbons considered here.
item.dc:creator: C. I. \'Avila-Joach\'in, J. C. Sandoval-Santana, Pedro Pereyra

item.title: Robustness of Skyrmion-Mediated Magnetization Switching in Perpendicular Magnetic Tunnel Junctions (p-MTJs) to Material Disorder and Elevated Temperature
item.description: arXiv:2610.32944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transient-skyrmion mediated voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) switching is a fast and energy efficient way to magnetization reversal, but its reliability under realistic material disorder and thermal fluctuations remain unclear. In this work, we use stochastic micromagnetic simulations of a 100 nm perpendicular magnetic tunnel junction to study switching reliability under grain-scale variations in Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, easy-axis orientation, and intergrain exchange coupling. We find that switching remains robust under moderate disorder, with 100% switching observed in 10^4 stochastic simulations after pulse width optimization at both 300 K and 350 K. Increasing the temperature from 300 to 350 K shifts the optimum VCMA pulse width from ~475 to ~450 ps, indicating that an apparent reduction in switching probability at a fixed pulse duration can be primarily due to pulse detuning. In contrast, strong easy-axis disorder reduces the maximum switching probability even after pulse-width optimization, indicating degradation of the switching dynamics. We further show that, under strong easy-axis disorder a transient skyrmion still forms while the subsequent post-pulse dynamics fails to complete the magnetization reversal. Our study therefore establishes the distinction between recoverable reliability due to timing shifts and permanent disorder-induced degradation that simply cannot be recovered by pulse re-tuning. Finally, for no disorders but at room temperature, 100% switching is observed with 10^6 stochastic simulations with correct pulse shaping.
item.dc:creator: Prosenjit Das, Md Mahadi Rajib, Jayasimha Atulasimha

item.title: Vacancy-driven topological transition of a Chern insulator
item.description: arXiv:2610.30241v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a microscopic description of the strong-disorder transition in a Chern insulator using the in-gap ring states bound to individual vacancies. Using Green's function formalism, we construct an energy-dependent Hamiltonian describing their hybridization. In a commensurate periodic vacancy lattice, a Dirac inversion of the zero-energy vacancy kernel accounts for the change in the occupied-state Chern number of the full system. We treat weak positional disorder using the self-consistent Born approximation and numerical disorder averaging, and study independently distributed vacancies using transfer-matrix and multifractal scaling. The local Chern marker and current textures track the transition in real space. Together, these results highlight the role that nonperturbative ring states have as microscopic degrees of freedom through which strong disorder destroys the Chern phase.
item.dc:creator: Peize Ding, Raquel Queiroz

item.title: Phonon evidence for a partial, re-entrant spin reorientation near room temperature in LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spin reorientation near room temperature offers a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order, yet LaFeO$3$, which lacks a magnetic rare-earth ion, is generally expected to retain its spin orientation along the $a$ axis below $T{\mathrm N}\approx740$~K. Here, we investigate LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$ ($x=0$ and 0.1) using temperature-dependent magnetization and Raman spectroscopy over 200--400~K. Both compositions exhibit magnetic anomalies at 285.6 and 323~K, respectively, accompanied by correlated deviations of 12 Raman modes from their conventional anharmonic behavior. Principal component analysis and a global fitting approach reveal a common temperature-dependent phonon response, with mode-dependent amplitudes and signs. To interpret these anomalies, we develop a Landau-based spin-phonon coupling model describing complete, partial re-entrant, and incipient spin reorientation. Comparison with the experimental Raman profiles favors a partial, re-entrant rotation of the N'eel vector in both compositions, centered near 290~K. Ni substitution narrows the characteristic reorientation interval from approximately 116 to 84~K and enhances the magnetization anomaly by a factor of four. An additional feature near 262~K in LaFeO$_3$ is consistent with the Morin transition of trace $\alpha$-Fe$_2$O$_3$. These findings suggest that partial spin reorientation can emerge without magnetic rare-earth ions and establish collective Raman phonon anomalies as a sensitive indirect probe of magnetic anisotropy changes in orthoferrites.
item.dc:creator: Subha Maity, Dushyant Singh, Vigneshwari S R, Tharundev V V, Navneet Sharma, Subhavenkadesh SS, Krista R. Khiangte

item.title: Strontium Titanate Capping Layers as Kinetic Regulators of Redox Phase Transitions in Oxide Heterostructures
item.description: arXiv:2610.31871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Oxide capping layers are widely used to protect and stabilize thin-film heterostructures, yet their role in governing phase-transition kinetics remains largely unexplored. Here, we uncover the kinetic function of few-nanometer-thick SrTiO$_3$ (STO) capping layers in controlling oxidation and reduction processes, using real-time in situ optical spectroscopic ellipsometry. We show that oxygen diffusion through the nanoscale capping layer constitutes the rate-limiting step, giving rise to diffusion-controlled phase transitions in the underlying materials. As a result, both capping-layer thickness and oxygen partial pressure provide effective handles to tune phase transition temperatures. Quantitative analysis yields an activation energy of $E_A$ = 0.64 $\pm$0.06 eV for oxygen diffusion through STO, highlighting its suitability for precise control of redox reactions in diverse material systems. These results establish oxide capping layers as active kinetic regulators of redox-driven phase transitions and offer a general framework for engineering redox dynamics in complex oxide heterostructures.
item.dc:creator: Pooya Abdollahi, Woo Jin Kim, Keaghan Knight, Harold Y. Hwang, Ambrose Seo

item.title: Intrinsic Paramagnetism of Optical Phonons and Thermal Hall Effect in Quantum Paraelectrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.32224v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a microscopic theory of the phonon-mediated thermal Hall effect in quantum paraelectrics, driven by the intrinsic paramagnetism due to quantum fluctuations of the (nearly) critical optical phonon modes. The effective magnetization due to temporal fluctuations of the assosciated dipoles couple to an external magnetic field resulting the magnetoelectric term $\mathbf{H} \cdot (\mathbf{P} \times \dot{\mathbf{P}})$ in the effective Lagrangian density of the polarisation field $\mathbf{P}$. This coupling splits the transverse optical phonon spectrum into right- and left-circularly polarized chiral branches. Using the chiral phonon Green's functions and the Kubo formalism, we derive the thermal Hall conductivity $\kappa_{xy}$ from the heat-current correlation function. We observe that $\kappa_{xy}$ is proportional to the difference in spectral weights of the two chiral modes, $\kappa_{xy} \propto A_+^2 - A_-^2$, establishing a direct microscopic link between phonon chirality and transverse heat transport. Our theory predicts three key observations: (i) a linear-in-magnetic-field response $\kappa_{xy} \propto H$ at low fields, evolving into nonlinear behavior at higher fields (ii) a non-monotonic temperature dependence of $\kappa_{xy}$ with a peak arising from the competition between thermal population and phonon scattering and (iii) strong enhancement of $\kappa_{xy}$ near the quantum critical point $\omega_0 \to 0$, it exhibits power-law scaling $\kappa_{xy} \propto T^{\alpha}$ with $\alpha \approx 0.41$. Our findings provide an understanding of thermal Hall transport in quantum paraelectrics due to intrinsic paramagnetism and is aligned with the observed behaviour in SrTiO$_3$ and related materials.
item.dc:creator: Harsh Jain, Manideep Gone, Nabyendu Das

item.title: Interface Control of Second-Harmonic Generation in Layered CuInP2S6 via PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 Domain Wall
item.description: arXiv:2610.32228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The control of nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale offers opportunities for developing two-dimensional integrated nanophotonics with programmable functionalities. In this work, we report the first realization of nanoscale nonvolatile control of the amplitude and polarization of second-harmonic generation (SHG) response in layered CuInP2S6 (CIPS) via the domain structure in an interfacial PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 (PZT) thin film. The SHG intensity at CIPS/PZT heterointerface is continuously modulated, either substantially enhanced or almost entirely quenched, by the circular domain walls in underlying ferroelectric oxide. The interfacial coupling of CIPS polar axis with in-plane polarization of PZT domain walls tailors the SHG light polarization into two-fold (C2V) symmetry, which is well modeled by nonlinear electromagnetic theory. Overall, this study enables nonvolatile programmable design of nonlinear light intensity and polarization in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale.
item.dc:creator: Dawei Li, Juhe Liu, Yifei Hao, Qiuchen Wu, Xi Huang, Jesse Stebbing, Xinyi Hou, Gaolei Zhao, Kun Wang, Yongfeng Lu, Xia Hong

item.title: Near-field maps of topological edge states of molecular aggregates
item.description: arXiv:2610.32287v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-assembled two-dimensional molecular aggregates provide a versatile platform for engineering excitonic states, including topologically nontrivial edge states. However, these edge-states are difficult to probe optically: they have weak far-field transition strengths, and far-field spectra do not reveal whether an excitation is localized at the edge. For an aggregate consisting of two sublattices of molecules with genuinely complex transition dipoles, we show that spatially resolved near-field spectroscopy encodes the full spatial structure of these states. The resulting near-field maps do not mirror the site populations, but instead exhibit strongly nonuniform, interference-like features. We demonstrate that a convolutional neural network can reconstruct the complex expansion coefficients of the eigenstates from these maps, and that this reconstruction is robust against substantial random noise.
item.dc:creator: Aritra Mishra, Sidhartha Nayak, Alexander Eisfeld

item.title: Finite-Temperature Transconductance of Multiterminal Josephson Junctions with Topological Andreev Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2610.32839v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) provide a controllable platform for engineering topological Andreev spectra. At zero temperature, Andreev bound states (ABSs) with nonzero Chern numbers give rise to quantized transconductance between superconducting terminals. We derive the finite-temperature transconductance of MTJJs using linear-response theory. We first demonstrate the destructive role of temperature: changes in the thermal occupations of the ABSs destroy exact transconductance quantization. We then show that finite temperature can also play a constructive role by making the transconductance sensitive to finite-energy topological crossings hidden from the zero-temperature response. Our results establish the thermal limitations of transconductance quantization and identify finite-temperature transport as a probe of otherwise inaccessible topology in Andreev spectra.
item.dc:creator: Gleb S. Seleznev, David C. Ohnmacht, Wolfgang Belzig

item.title: Extended Hydrodynamics of Planar Heisenberg Ferromagnetic Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Access to hydro and quasi-hydro regimes in magnetic systems is steadily increasing with the advances in fabrication of clean materials, and motivates study of hydrodynamics beyond conventional regimes and probe non-equilibrium transport. We employ the framework of extended irreversible thermodynamics which includes dynamical dissipative currents as quasi-hydro variables, and effect the modified hydrodynamic equations suitable to describe planar Heisenberg ferromagnetic systems in both paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases. We show that the new transport coefficients and relaxation time scales introduced by quasi-hydro variables can engineer diverse combination of dispersion relations and provide control over the nature of hydrodynamic modes. For instance, we can change the diffusive energy mode into propagating one in multiple ways, including by tuning the relaxation time of magnetization current.
item.dc:creator: Dwigbijoy Paul, Sreedhar B. Dutta

item.title: Kagome goldene with flat bands and Dirac nodal line fermions via line-graph epitaxy
item.description: arXiv:2503.07945v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The kagome lattice has emerged as a promising platform for investigating exotic quantum phases. However, achieving a single-atomic-layer kagome lattice in elemental materials remains a significant challenge. Here, we introduce line-graph epitaxy, a novel approach that enables the atomic-scale synthesis of goldene, a monolayer of elemental gold atoms arranged in a kagome lattice. Through scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we demonstrate the formation of kagome goldene, featuring a flat band with a van Hove singularity approximately 1.1 eV below the Fermi level, signaling strong electron correlation effects. Notably, the flat band is disrupted at the zigzag edges of goldene nanoflakes, revealing substantial edge effects. Furthermore, our calculations show that weak interlayer interactions between goldene and the underlying Au2Ge substrate generate dual Dirac nodal lines through a proximity effect. These findings offer not only a novel strategy for constructing elemental kagome lattices, but also a generalizable framework for fabricating and controlling line-graph materials. This research advances the exploration of quantum phases driven by strong correlations and the design of materials for next-generation quantum technologies.
item.dc:creator: Qiwei Tian, Sahar Izadi Vishkayi, Chen Zhang, Jiang Zeng, Bo Li, Li Zhang, Long-Jing Yin, Yuan Tian, Meysam Bagheri Tagani, Lijie Zhang, Zhihui Qin

item.title: Identification and mitigation of errors in hole spin qubit readout
item.description: arXiv:2504.06898v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-fidelity readout of spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots can be achieved by combining a radiofrequency charge sensor with spin-to-charge conversion and Pauli spin blockade. However, reaching high readout fidelities with hole spin qubits remains challenging due to site-dependent spin anisotropies and short relaxation times during readout. Here, we analyze the multiple error processes that arise during readout using a double-latched scheme in a germanium double quantum dot hole spin qubit system. We first investigate the spin-to-charge conversion process as a function of magnetic field orientation, and configure the system to adiabatically map the $\lvert \downarrow\downarrow \rangle$ state to the only non-blockaded state. We reveal a strong magnetic field strength dependence of the spin relaxation rates, and minimize it by operating at low fields. We further characterize and mitigate the error processes that arise during the double-latching process. By combining a radiofrequency charge sensor, a double-latching process, and optimized magnetic field parameters, we achieve a single-shot single-qubit state-preparation-and-measurement fidelity of 97.0% while maintaining control of both spins under the readout conditions.

item.title: Hidden chirality and half-vortex formation in exciton-polariton condensates
item.description: arXiv:2606.16233v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that a radially symmetric, nonresonantly pumped spinor exciton-polariton condensate can acquire chirality without a rotating drive, chiral geometry, or pump orbital angular momentum. Spin relaxation in a two-reservoir system shifts the reservoir-induced blueshift relative to the gain profile, creating an effective non-Hermitian chiral potential. A reduced angular-mode theory reveals tunable exceptional points and non-reciprocal coupling between counter-rotating modes. Full driven-dissipative Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that this hidden chirality enables all-optical formation of spin-selective half-vortices.
item.dc:creator: A. N. Osipov, I. Y. Chestnov, P. G. Lagoudakis, A. V. Yulin

item.title: Chirality-induced spin selectivity due to an emergent molecular orbital moment
item.description: arXiv:2606.17865v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The microscopic origin of chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS), a phenomena where chiral molecules connected to a magnetic electrode show large spin-dependent conductance asymmetry even in ambient temperature, still remains an open question. Most of the existent theories are based on some sort of effective spin-orbit coupling or interfacial scattering, which do not provide satisfactory explanations for experimental observations such as the magnitude of spin polarization or the length dependence of the effect. We propose an alternative theoretical framework rooted in an intrinsic molecular contribution that shows a robust CISS effect and scales with the length of the molecule. The mechanism is based on the emergent molecular magnetic moment (MOM), which can produce experimentally observed point-symmetric I-V curves without violating the Onsager-Casimir reciprocity relation. The MOM has an intrinsic component that is governed by the chirality of the molecule and leads to finite CISS magnetoresistance and magnetochiral conductance asymmetry (MChA) that are even in bias voltage. By decomposing the MOM into its Fermi sea and Fermi surface components, we show that under strong bias, the MOM can be dominated by the Fermi surface contribution, which causes a sign change in the MChA leading to a behavior similar to that of electric magnetochiral anisotropy (eMChA). Finally, we analyze the effect of a magnetic field within the same framework, which may provide better insight into the crossover between CISS and eMChA.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Ghosh, Angela Wittmann, Frank Matthes, Daniel E. B\"urgler

item.title: Driven square lattice of quantum dots in a magnetic field coupled to a cylindrical FIR-photon cavity
item.description: arXiv:2607.06812v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a comprehensive computational study of driven quantum dot arrays in a square lattice configuration, subject to an external magnetic field and coupled to a cylindrical far-infrared photon cavity. The driving is introduced through a harmonic modulation of the full electron-photon interaction, therefore including both paramagnetic and diamagnetic contributions. The electron-electron Coulomb interactions are treated within density functional theory, while the electron-photon coupling is modeled using a many-body configuration interaction approach at each iteration of the density functional. By exploiting the unique properties of the cylindrical TE$_{011}$ cavity mode, we demonstrate selective enhancement of diamagnetic two-photon transitions. Our results reveal that the effectiveness of harmonic modulation of the electron-photon interaction is strongly dependent on both the driving frequency and the electron occupation number per dot. When the driving frequency approaches twice the cavity photon frequency, the system exhibits resonant behavior characterized by efficient photon pumping, occupation of higher-order photon replicas, and activation of collective radial Coulomb breathing modes. These findings establish a controllable mechanism for manipulating photon states in coupled quantum dot-cavity systems and provide insights into the interplay among harmonic modulation, photonic excitations, magnetic confinement, and many-body electron correlations in dimensionally reduced nanostructures.
item.dc:creator: Vidar Gudmundsson, Vram Mughnetsyan, Hsi-Sheng Goan, Jeng-Da Chai, Nzar Rauf Abdullah, Chi-Shung Tang, Wen-Hsuan Kuan, Valeriu Moldoveanu, Andrei Manolescu

item.title: Visualizing Chiral Edge Modes in Twisted Cuprate Superconductors via Scanning-Probe Quantum Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2609.13070v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently, unconventional superconductivity hosted by twisted van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures has received immense interest due to the exotic pairing symmetry, electronic interactions and nontrivial topological nature that are naturally relevant to the fast-advancing quantum technologies. Here, we report scanning-probe quantum sensing of nanoscale electromagnetic behaviors of twisted vdW cuprate superconductors. Using single-spin relaxometry, we directly visualize edge modes spontaneously formed in twisted Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x (BSCCO). By investigating temperature dependent variations of edge-state-induced quantum spin relaxation, we experimentally evaluate the magnitude of nontrivial topological band gap opened at nodal points in twisted BSCCO and its critical temperature behaviors under different twist angles. We further observe alternating chiral domains defined by edge modes, exploring experimental signatures of in-plane magnetic field-induced topology in 45{\deg} twisted BSCCO. Our results advance the current understanding of twisted vdW nodal superconductors, presenting an appealing high-temperature topological superconducting material platform for cutting-edge quantum innovation.
item.dc:creator: Senlei Li, Xiaomeng Cui, Renzhi Sun, Lingjie Zhou, Yiran Zhao, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Genda Gu, Hailong Wang, Kartiek Agarwal, Philip Kim, Chunhui Rita Du

item.title: Laser-induced metastable (anti-)skyrmion states with higher-order topological charge
item.description: arXiv:2609.13112v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ultrafast creation and manipulation of topologically non-trivial spin objects promises significant potential for spintronic applications. Here, we demonstrate laser-induced nucleation of skyrmions and antiskyrmions with topological charge up to $|Q|=3$ from the saturated magnetization state of a Co/Ni-multilayer which does not intrinsically host a skyrmionic ground state. The resulting configuration of spin objects thus constitutes a metastable, thermodynamically hidden magnetic state. We control the number and type of spin objects by the excitation fluence and the external out-of-plane magnetic field.

item.title: Unmodeled states and uncertain action outcomes in agentic scanning tunneling microscopy
item.description: arXiv:2609.27302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In physical experiments, interventions can alter hidden experimental states in ways that cannot be predicted in advance. Autonomous scientific agents must therefore interpret the consequences of their interventions while operating with incomplete knowledge of the experimental state. Here we investigate this problem using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) tip conditioning, traditionally a human-expert-intensive task governed by inaccessible tip apex conditions and uncertain action outcomes. We introduce quailbot, an agent harness that places the LLM inside the instrument feedback loop by linking physical interventions with experimental readbacks. After a brief apprenticeship with a human expert, frontier LLM agents autonomously completed end-to-end tip conditioning on an STM and passed an independent verification. The contingencies that arose during the experiments further exposed the limits of LLM agentic autonomy when relevant experimental states or dynamics were hidden or unmodeled. Our results show that future autonomous physical experimentation requires agents to infer hidden and unmodeled experimental states, track the outcomes of their actions, and operate within the observability and action limits of real instruments.
item.dc:creator: Siyu Cheng, Muxian Xu, Christopher Candelora, Ilija Zeljkovic

item.title: Arbitrary-order exceptional points in a nanomechanical cavity
item.description: arXiv:2512.11679v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Exceptional points (EPs), non-Hermitian spectral singularities, shape the evolution dynamics ranging from topological mode control to high-precision sensing. Higher-order EPs unlock enriched and sharpened spectral topology beyond the minimal second-order counterpart, thus expanding capabilities in those domains. However, the intrinsic topological fragility of higher-order EPs has long hindered their robust experimental realization. Here, we present a scalable architecture that implements arbitrary-order EPs via an optically mediated recurrent network comprising a single nanomechanical resonator and an ensemble of digital synthetic resonators. We experimentally validate this architecture's scalability for both linear and nonlinear mechanical EPs, demonstrating EPs up to the seventh order. Moreover, we reveal that the fundamental noise component, in contrast to some technical-noise contributions, shares the same system coupling channel and undergoes identical root-response amplification as the measured signal. The co-amplification mechanism sets the fundamental sensitivity limit near EPs of any order, as verified by direct signal-to-noise ratio measurements. Our work establishes a general platform for exploring higher-order EP-based phenomena while clarifying the fundamental boundary of non-Hermitian sensitivity enhancement. More broadly, it facilitates a connection between non-Hermitian physics and AI-inspired recurrent architectures across diverse physical systems.
item.dc:creator: Ning Wu, Kaiyu Cui, Ziming Chen, Chenxuan Wang, Xue Feng, Fang Liu, Wei Zhang, Hao Sun, Yongzhuo Li, Yidong Huang

item.title: Unifying description of competing chiral and nematic superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene
item.description: arXiv:2603.06550v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reveal a striking correspondence between electron- and phonon-driven pairing in twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) by mapping an atomistic electronically driven pairing model onto an effective inter-valley, intra-Chern description, originally proposed for phonon-mediated superconductivity. Within the unified framework of intra-Chern pairing, we then analyze the competition between nematic and chiral $d$-wave superconducting states. The latter corresponds to the extreme Chern-polarized limit and hosts unpaired flat bands within the superconducting gap, which generally disfavors it relative to the nematic states. Crucially, nematic order is locally preferred at each momentum, but the optimal nematic directions are incompatible across the Brillouin zone due to the broken rotation symmetry. This momentum-space frustration still enables a chiral ground state at large fillings or weak interactions in a symmetric parent state. Including heterostrain or inter-valley coherence further stabilizes the nematic ground state and sets the nematic direction. Under heterostrain, this direction shows a double winding with the strain axis, revealing the $d$-wave nature of the pairing, while inter-valley coherence makes it filling dependent. Our results thereby provide a unified understanding of superconductivity in TBG, in which electron- and phonon-mediated pairing cooperate, and clarify the microscopic origin of the competition between the chiral and nematic superconducting states.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Baldo, Patric Holmvall, Annica M. Black-Schaffer
